title: Worksheet 12: The CPU
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: The Central Processing Unit, or CPU, is often called the "brain" of a computer because it is responsible for carrying out instructions and performing calculations. Every time a computer runs a program, whether it's opening an app, doing math, or displaying a picture, the CPU is the part doing the actual work of processing that information. The CPU is a small chip, but it can perform billions of calculations every second. Modern CPUs often contain multiple "cores," which act like separate mini-processors inside the same chip. Having multiple cores allows a computer to work on more than one task at the same time, which is called multitasking. The speed of a CPU is often measured in gigahertz (GHz), which describes how many cycles, or basic operations, the CPU can complete each second. A higher GHz number generally means the CPU can process instructions faster.
